title: A process-level uncaught exception constructs the record, emits it, and terminates cleanly with exit 1
asA: operator running the application under a supervising process
iWant: an uncaught exception to construct the internal record via TAC-1702, emit it through the logging companion at error level, and terminate with exit 1
soThat: the crash is diagnosable from one log line and the supervisor knows to restart the process

acceptanceCriteria.description: An uncaughtException on the Node runtime (or an equivalent unhandled error on another runtime) causes the process-level boundary to construct the internal record with category unknown when no code path set one, emit it as one JSON line at error level with the stack trace on cause, and exit the process with code 1.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application with the process-level boundary registered
acceptanceCriteria.when: an uncaught exception is thrown from any code path
acceptanceCriteria.then: one log line is emitted at error level with the record shape (code, category unknown, message, correlationId, cause, context), and process.exitCode equals 1

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an unhandled promise rejection fires on the process (a rejected Promise with no `.catch` handler), when the process-level boundary observes the event, then one error record is written under the `unknown` category with the rejection value serialised as its cause, and the process terminates with exit code 1.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process with the error-handling boundary armed and a promise rejection with no attached handler
acceptanceCriteria.then: one record under category `unknown` is written and the process exits with code 1

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the process-level boundary is registered and a code path deliberately calls `process.exit(0)` (a clean shutdown from elsewhere in the application), when the process exits, then the boundary does NOT construct a record and does NOT override the exit code to 1; the clean-shutdown path is preserved and only uncaughtException / unhandledRejection paths coerce to exit 1.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process-level boundary registered and a code path calling process.exit(0)
acceptanceCriteria.then: no record is constructed, no exit-code override fires, and the clean-shutdown code 0 is preserved

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given two uncaughtException events fire in quick succession (a rare double-throw during shutdown), when the process-level boundary observes them, then TWO records are constructed and emitted through the logging companion in order (one per event); the process still terminates cleanly with exit 1; no recursive re-entry into the boundary constructs a third record.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two uncaughtException events firing in quick succession
acceptanceCriteria.then: two records emit in order through the logging companion, the process exits 1 cleanly, and no re-entry constructs a third record

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the process-level boundary is registered under a browser runtime (rather than Node), when an equivalent unhandled error fires (`window.error` / `window.unhandledrejection`), the boundary constructs the internal record via TAC-1702 the same way, emits it through the logging companion, and does NOT attempt to call `process.exit` (which does not exist in the browser); the applying project's guide names the browser-runtime path.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a browser runtime with the boundary registered and an unhandled error firing
acceptanceCriteria.then: a record is constructed and emitted; no process.exit call is attempted; the browser-runtime path is honoured
